title: Electronic Payment System for Work Permit Holders
what_it_is: Electronic Payment System for Work Permit Holders

sections.label: Electronic salary payment flexibility concerns
sections.summary: Two-thirds of workers receive salaries electronically, and MOM introduced an online facility in October 2014 for employers to open bank accounts for Work Permit holders.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpowe)
sentences.text: Today, two-thirds of these workers already receive their salaries electronically.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpowe)
sentences.text: To enhance this further, since October 2014, Ministry of Manpower (MOM) has introduced an online facility to allow employers to open bank accounts for their Work Permit holders automatically when they apply for their Work Permits.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpowe)
sentences.text: However, during consultations with unions, workers and employers, some have expressed a preference for flexibility.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpowe)
sentences.text: So, some workers have also preferred to receive their salaries in cash.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpowe)
sentences.text: They say they will face difficulties in maintaining a minimum sum account balance, as required by the banks, or be charged a fee, if their bank accounts do not meet the minimum sum requirement.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpowe)
sentences.text: Similarly, some small and micro-SME employers like family-run shops, also expressed difficulties in paying salaries electronically as they would need to incur additional administrative costs and resources to perform this task.

sections.label: Existing law on electronic payment
sections.summary: Employers must provide electronic payment if workers request it, and workers can approach MOM if salaries are late or incomplete.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: Under our existing law, we have already mandated employers to make electronic payment provision mandatory for the workers, if they make the request.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
sentences.text: If workers find that their salaries are not paid on time or not paid in full sum per their contract, they can always approach MOM for assistance.
